summary: The group is the weakest kind of picture on the site for card interaction: 13 of 27 runs scrub a `Data:` knob (noise, contrast, tract count) and 6 more scrub by full rebuild, while most operations have no spatial handle and are better served by `probe` (hover a point or tract to see its neighbors and its statistic). The best pictures are the tract maps (empirical Bayes trio, segregation, similar-locations), emerging-hot-spots and spatial-scan-statistic, which fill the frame and read without explanation. The worst are the scalar-summary runs (gamma-statistic, spatial-pearson, global-spatial-statistics, mantel-test, knox-test), where a lone bar or a mixed-unit summary buffer is drawn as bars with no reference, and nested-interpolation-validation, whose scatter appears to include unpredicted (zero) training rows. Eleven runs share `shared/point-field.ts`: the Carolina rainfall extract sits in the middle third of the frame (the rest is black) and the lower 36% is reserved for a chart that often holds one bar, so a single fit-to-frame change there fixes `small` across the cluster. Knox and Mantel share `createSpaceTimeEvents`, whose Kilauea epicenters collapse into one tiny blob; zooming to the dense area would make both readable. Several local statistics look alike (local Geary, multivariate Geary, LOSH; local permutation, LOSH permutation, multivariate Geary test; the two empirical Bayes runs), and a shared probe that highlights the hovered point's neighbors (edges are already built by `createWeightEdges`) would both distinguish them and explain the weights. The one natural `place` entry is similar-locations, whose reference tract is already written per frame but is exposed only as a `Data:` slider.

sharedChanges.change: Fit the rainfall-station extract to the full world width (or crop to the station bounds) in createPointField, and drop the reserved CHART_BAND when the chart is a single scalar, so the map fills the card instead of its middle third.
Add getNeighborRows(graph, row) / neighbor-edge subset for a hovered point, reusing createWeightEdges, so every weights-based run can probe its neighborhood with one helper.
createSpaceTimeEvents: project to the bounds of the dense epicenter cluster (quantile bounds, outliers clamped to the edge) so the events fill the map instead of a 20 px blob.

Add a tract hit test (point-in-tract via the triangle mesh or nearest center) and rook-neighbor lookup from tracts.contiguity, and lower the default populationScale used by the rate runs so shrinkage is visible.

One chart helper that draws a reference distribution as a histogram with a vertical marker at the observed value and the pseudo p-value as readout, replacing scatter-versus-index plots and mixed-unit summary bars.

frameworkNeeds: defineOperationRun pointer hook (pointer in world coordinates -> parameter patch and/or highlight state), the run-level equivalent of GpuSceneInstance.setPointer
pointer to nearest point lookup over a positions buffer (CPU copy) and pointer to tract polygon hit test
highlight subset on dots and polygons layers (index list or uint32 mask buffer), plus an edges overlay for a hovered node's neighbors
glyphs at the pointer: ring of a world radius, crosshair, vertical/horizontal line, curtain line
per-layer clip rectangle for swipe (left of x draws layer A, right draws layer B)
value under pointer readout: CPU readback of a per-element output buffer for the hovered row
chart reference marks: zero line, expected value line, vertical marker at an observed value, histogram buffer with explicit xRange
row offset / slice on a layer's values buffer (draw fold k of a fold-major buffer)
snapped, debounced rebuild for pointer-driven compile-time props, or pre-built variants keyed by value
small inset chart (sparkline) for a hovered cell's series from a slice of an output buffer
